errors.sentence: She don't like coffee in the morning.
errors.explanation: With he, she and it we use doesn't in the present simple.

errors.sentence: Yesterday we goed to the beach.
errors.explanation: Go is irregular: the past simple is went.

errors.sentence: If I will see him, I will tell him.
errors.explanation: In the if-clause of the first conditional we use the present simple.

errors.sentence: My brother is more taller than me.
errors.explanation: Short adjectives take -er; do not add more.

errors.sentence: I have lived here since five years.
errors.explanation: Use for with a period of time and since with a starting point.

errors.sentence: There are much cats in my street.
errors.explanation: Cats are countable, so we use many.
After modal verbs like can we use the base form of the verb.

errors.sentence: I have seen that movie yesterday.
errors.explanation: With a finished time like yesterday we use the past simple, not the present perfect.

errors.sentence: There is many people at the party.
errors.explanation: People is plural, so we say there are.

errors.sentence: This is the most good restaurant in town.
errors.explanation: Good is irregular: the superlative is the best.

errors.sentence: I am agree with your opinion.
errors.explanation: Agree is a verb, so we do not use am before it.
After doesn't we use the base form of the verb, without -s.

errors.sentence: We arrived to the airport at six.
errors.explanation: We arrive at a place (or in a city), never to a place.

errors.sentence: She bought an uniform for school.
errors.explanation: Uniform starts with a "you" sound, so we use a, not an.

errors.sentence: Listen! The baby cry in the other room.
errors.explanation: Listen! shows the action is happening now, so we use the present continuous.

errors.sentence: My aunt is married with a doctor.
errors.explanation: We say married to someone, not married with someone.
